BC_description: The methods async.applyEach and async.applyEachSeries have been changed. They now always return a function that accepts a single callback argument. If this callback is omitted, the returned function becomes awaitable via Promise. Crucially, the partial application feature previously available in applyEach—where additional arguments could be bound to the function—has been removed. Functions returned from applyEach and applyEachSeries no longer support partial argument application; only a callback or .then/await Promise is supported. The method signature and return value shape are changed: previous usage passing arguments for partial application will break. For example, before: async.applyEach(fns, arg1, arg2, cb); now: const fn = async.applyEach(fns); fn(cb) or await fn().
